newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore pager price war as SingTel cuts rates.
newsitem.headline: Singapore pager price war as SingTel cuts rates.

text.p: Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel) undercut all its new domestic competitors on Friday by reducing its basic paging prices by more than 35 percent, state television reported.
It said SingTel had cut monthly subscription rates for its numeric paging service to Singapore $9.50 from S$15.00 -- but only for subscribers signing up for a two-year contract.
The cut puts SingTel's rates below its three competitors, who entered the Singapore paging market when it was deregulated on April 1.
Hutchison Paging currently charges S$9.90 a month for a similar service, while Sunpage charges S$9.80 and MobileOne's fess are S$14.00.
State television quoted SingTel's competitors as saying they would stick to their current charges "for the moment".
After 10 days of operations, Hutchison claimed to have gained 15,000 subscribers and Sunpage 24,000 users, it said, adding that MobileOne had declined to disclose its figures.
State television gave no further details.
SingTel officials were unavailable for immediate comment.
Hutchison Paging is a joint venture of Hong Kong's Hutchison Whampoa, Intraco and Teledata.

Sunpage is a unit of state-owned conglomerate Singapore Technologies. MobileOne is a joint venture of Keppel Telecom, Singapore Press Holdings, Britain's Cable & Wireless and Hong Kong Telecommunications.
